reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it teaches viewers how to create and configure an Amazon Associates account and explains affiliate compensation from purchases made through Amazon links. The described activity is an ordinary affiliate arrangement rather than an investment deposit, required payment, or credential request directed at viewers.

opening.argument: Judge, this is more than an explanation of affiliate links. The speaker asks how viewers can “gain money for free” and says he will show them how to make an account and receive payment. He then demonstrates account creation and tells viewers they can create their own Payoneer account through a link in the description. That joins an easy-income pitch to a registration and payment-account pathway. Showing the steps does not erase the solicitation; it makes the promised income feel immediately actionable.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that the video demonstrates account setup and product links. But those examples do not answer what the viewer is being encouraged to expect from completing the setup. The speaker explicitly introduces the process with a question about gaining money “for free,” then directs viewers through account creation. The absence of an investment deposit does not settle whether this is an easy-income solicitation.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted question about money “for free” does not establish that viewers are promised a payment merely for registering. The speaker describes earning through an affiliate link when a customer buys a product, and demonstrates creating such a link. The account and payment steps are part of that operational walkthrough, not evidence of a separate reward for signing up.

opening.argument: Judge, consider the income claims together. The speaker presents an alleged monthly earning as proof, asks how to gain money “for free,” and later describes an “80%” affiliate return when someone buys through a link. He also presses viewers to watch to the end, saying they will otherwise never understand the process. The record does not independently establish the earnings or the stated return. Those claims give the account tutorial a more enticing, lower-barrier financial impression than the mechanics alone would convey.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense identifies a real tutorial, but demonstrating where to create a link does not substantiate the earnings shown or explain the apparent “80%” claim. Its account of compensation as purchases through links addresses the basic mechanism, not the reliability of the financial impression used to attract viewers. Nor does the lack of a requested deposit resolve whether an unusually easy return is being promoted.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The suspect figures are reasons to scrutinize the explanation, but they do not turn the demonstrated activity into a promised payout for a simple viewer action. The speaker ties earnings to a customer choosing to buy through an Amazon link and shows how to create a product link. The opening offers no evidence that merely watching, registering, or clicking yields the cited income.

opening.argument: Judge, the tutorial framing also serves a promotional path. The description promises to help viewers make money online and sends them to a separate account-opening video. In the walkthrough, the speaker says the account can be connected to Payoneer and directs viewers to his description link to create one. At the close, he encourages viewers to share the video with people seeking affiliate income. Those invitations matter: the lesson does not merely describe a business model, but moves an income-seeking audience toward additional account setup and circulation of the pitch.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense's examples of account fields and microphone-link creation show that instruction occurs; they do not make the surrounding invitations irrelevant. The same material directs viewers to another account-opening resource and connects account setup with earning online. A working tutorial can still function as a funnel. The issue is the cumulative direction of the message, not whether any one screen is fabricated.

citations.quote: See how to open a Pioneer account: https://youtu.be/nbwtnivie5s
This amazon affiliate marketing tutorial 2020 will helps you make money online.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion and instruction are not mutually exclusive, but the cited invitations do not show a deceptive reward or a payment to the creator. The video walks through Amazon Associates information, including a website or app used to display links, and then demonstrates generating a product link. A related payment-account resource does not by itself change that ordinary affiliate workflow into a scam.
